Subject: Initial MAP draft and security checklist for NimbusBank evaluation

Hi Samira —

Thanks again for the time yesterday. Attached is an initial Mutual Onboarding Plan (MAP) we sketched for NimbusBank that includes the security/compliance gates we typically tie to an evaluation: SOC 2 report, SIG/CAIQ mapping, DPA negotiation, and explicit data-retention windows for logs and user data.

Quick summary of what we need to align on so we can land the evaluation timeline:
- SOC 2: do you need our full report (typical) or a scoped bridge letter?
- SIG/CAIQ: we can provide completed CAIQ answers + evidence samples.
- DPA: we'll share a standard Redwood DPA; let us know any non-starter clauses.
- Retention: default token/log retention is 90 days; we support shorter windows for regulated workloads. Need to confirm Nimbus requirements for PII vs non-PII storage.

Proposed evaluation + close timeline (subject to your legal/security review):
- Week 0: Exchange MAP and evidence; DPA redline kickoff
- Week 1–2: Security deep-dive and SIG/CAIQ Q&A
- Week 2–3: Pilot (sandbox) with sample traffic; SOC 2 bridge/summary shared
- Week 3: Mutual decision and contract signature (DocuSign link)

I've attached Nimbus-MAP-v0.9.pdf for your review. Can you and Oliver confirm who from Nimbus will lead the technical and legal reviews? If 2-week eval looks tight, we can extend slightly but prefer to keep momentum.

Thanks —
Neha Kapoor

Neha / Marissa —

Quick technical run-down to send back to Nimbus:
- SOC 2: we can provide the full SOC 2 Type II report for 2026. If Nimbus requires faster evidence, we can also supply a bridge letter summarizing no changes in control posture since the last report. Attached: SOC2-summary-2026.pdf.
- CAIQ: completed CAIQ answers are available; we'll export the answers and include evidence pointers for ~18 control areas relevant to data handling and encryption.
- Retention: Redwood supports per-tenant retention for audit logs in our private and dedicated deployments. For Hosted API customers, retention is set per account and can be configured during onboarding. Default: 90 days; available options: 30 / 90 / 180 / custom (negotiable).
- Data segregation: PII is tagged and stored separately; we can enable immediate purging of PII artifacts after configured window.
- Subprocessors: full list available — we can provide SOC2 mappings for critical subprocessors on request.

Suggested collateral to share now: SOC2-summary-2026.pdf, and a short doc outlining retention toggles (data-retention-options.md).

If legal needs specific wording for per-customer retention in the DPA, give me the text and I can advise on technical feasibility.

— Jonas

Subject: Re: Fwd: Nimbus MAP asks — legal / DPA redline notes

Neha / team —

Read Nimbus's spreadsheet and Jonas's notes. High-level legal position for the DPA:
- Data residency: we can contractually commit to processing in US regions for Nimbus's production workload; include language for future region requests.
- Retention: agree to a contractual option to set a 30-day retention for audit logs tied to PII. We'll flag language to ensure logs needed for incident analysis (short‑lived) are excluded or captured with customer consent.
- Subprocessors: provide notice + 30-day review window for new critical subprocessors.
- Liability: our standard caps apply; for enterprise deals we can entertain a higher cap tied to committed spend.

I'm attaching a preliminary redline (DPA-redline-nb.docx) with comments on the clauses Nimbus usually asks about. Recommend we offer a DPA addendum that addresses the 30-day PII audit-log retention, and reserve SOC 2 obligations as evidence rather than contractual warranties.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
